title: Significance: the $\alpha_{EM}$ shift chain and the atomic-braid shift framework share one combinatorial primitive
html:
Remark. Significance: the \alpha_{EM} shift chain and the atomic-braid shift framework share one combinatorial primitive

Significance: bridge to the atomic-shift framework. Both factors in the multiplicative chain (\alpha_{EM} shift multiplicative chain) expose the identical combinatorial primitive: the pole order at q = 0 of a seminormal Hecke trace.

Object Shift role
Atomic Markov-trace denominator D(u) = 2^{2A+1} \cdot u^{\mathrm{shift}} \cdot (1 + u^2)^{3A-1}
Torus knot T_{p,k} on V_{(1^p)} \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{p,k}) = k(p-1) (prop:alpha-shift-torus-knot)
Inverse fine-structure constant \alpha_{EM}^{-1} = q \cdot [\alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{2,9})]_q \cdot [\alpha_{\mathrm{shift}}(T_{3,5})]_q

The torus-braid case provides the clean limit of the atomic-braid shift framework. It restricts generators to \sigma_i alone, avoiding averaged or inverse generators. It eliminates inter-nucleon terms. It prevents within-partition Hecke \sigma^2-cancellation, because the standard Young tableau path through the single column occupies distinct axial distances at every step. It precludes cross-partition Ocneanu cancellation, because the maximum localises on a unique irreducible representation.
